target_customer: Pharmaceutical companies that co-develop or license the device for chronic injectables, and patients who self-inject; also military and first responder segments
problem: Self-injection with traditional auto-injectors is intimidating and hard for untrained users, which hurts adherence. Pirouette builds a low-profile push-button disc injector with a hidden needle.
business_model: Medical device and drug-device platform: co-development and licensing with pharma plus own 505(b)(2) and 351(k) programs

education: PhD in Medical Engineering and Medical Physics, MIT and Harvard Medical School (Health Sciences and Technology)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page. No prior employers listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: A rugged, patented disc-shaped injector with hidden needle and controlled insertion is a hardware device needing FDA device and combination product pathways, which is hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: The company holds patents on the device (patent listings found) and regulatory approvals take years, though large device makers such as BD and Ypsomed hold stronger positions.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. Incumbents developed their own wearable injectors, and Pirouette stayed independent as of the sources found.

market_need_then: Self-injected biologics and chronic therapies were growing and needle fear affects adherence, and the founders applied for NIH-backed work on a naloxone auto-injector for opioid overdose. No quantified market data was gathered.

branding.brand_signature: Tagline about making injections as easy as pushing a button
branding.community_and_virality: A Wefunder campaign drew over 4,000 investors and was billed by Wefunder as its largest raise (company and Wefunder claims).

brand_strength.rationale: The retail crowdfunding community of thousands of investors shows a following, but no independent press on the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Pirouette remains active and has funded itself largely through retail crowdfunding, with a 2024 Wefunder round led by Safar Partners alongside Y Combinator. Its progress depends on regulatory milestones and pharma partners, with targets claimed for 2027 to 2029. No exit or shutdown was found.
notes: The May 2024 round is reported by a Business Wire release and Pulse 2.0 as over $5M raised and described there as heading to a record community round of $7.8M; the $5M figure is the amount at the release date and the final size may be higher. Aggregators give conflicting later totals ($21.1M to $23.76M) and valuations ($55M to $95M), and a $4.3M second community round and a $4.1M February 2026 crowdfund are mentioned only by aggregators, so they are unverified and not recorded. Directories place the company in Portsmouth, NH while YC lists Boston. Business Wire fetch was blocked (403), so details come from search snippets. No dated competitor source near 2021 was found; Enable Injections, Ypsomed and BD sources are dated 2017 to 2025 only.
